I diagnosed the issue and verified the fix end-to-end in throwaway repos. Solution written to `/home/kara/solution.md`.

## Summary

**Root cause:** `.gitreins/` mixes a tracked contract with local runtime state. `.gitreins/config.yaml` is meant to be tracked, but `history/`, `verdicts/`, `tasks.yaml`, `tasks.yaml.lock`, `logs/`, and `usage.jsonl` are regenerated every guard tick. The repo added the config without the matching `.gitignore` rules, so git reports them as untracked forever and `git add -A` can commit them.

**Fix:** add explicit ignore lines (not a blanket `.gitreins/`) and commit them in the same commit as the guard config:

```gitignore
# .gitreins local runtime state (the guard contract stays tracked)
.gitreins/history/
.gitreins/verdicts/
.gitreins/tasks.yaml
.gitreins/tasks.yaml.lock
.gitreins/logs/
.gitreins/usage.jsonl
```

**Verified in a fresh repo:**
- `git ls-files .gitreins` → only `.gitreins/config.yaml`
- `git status --short` → empty
- `git add -A` then `git status --short` → still empty
- `git check-ignore -v` confirms each runtime path is matched by the new rules

The doc also covers the already-committed case (`git rm -r --cached ...`, keeping working copies on disk and leaving `config.yaml` tracked), which I verified leaves a clean status.

signatures.description: A repo adopts .gitreins/config.yaml but not the ignore rules for the guard's local runtime state, so git status --short shows tasks.yaml, tasks.yaml.lock, usage.jsonl and history/ as untracked on every tick and a later `git add -A` commits them. Fleet convention (verified on three siblings): .gitreins/config.yaml IS tracked (it is the guard contract); .gitreins/{history,verdicts,tasks.yaml,tasks.yaml.lock,logs,usage.jsonl} are local and must be gitignored. Fix by adding those lines to .gitignore and confirming git status --short is empty. Check this in the same commit that adds the guard config.
